purpose: Add eight source-exact Horatius Bonar excerpts for pastoral self-examination and sermon preparation.

defaults.author: Horatius Bonar
defaults.sourceTitle: Words to the Winners of Souls
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1860 American Tract Society edition is public domain; each excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the scan before publication.

entries.title: The object of Christian ministry
entries.text: We take for granted that the object of the Christian ministry is to convert sinners and to edify the body of Christ.
entries.slideText: We take for granted that the object of the Christian ministry is to convert sinners and to edify the body of Christ.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed ministry-purpose statement before teaching evangelism and edification from Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: The wording summarizes Bonar's pastoral priorities. Define conversion, ministry, and edification from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: If souls are not won
entries.text: If souls are not won, if saints are not matured, our ministry itself is vain.
entries.slideText: If souls are not won, if saints are not matured, our ministry itself is vain.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed challenge to keep Gospel ministry aimed at conversion and mature discipleship.
entries.reviewNote: God gives the increase; numerical outcomes are not fully controlled by the preacher. Balance Bonar's urgency with the cited KJV texts.

entries.title: Without actual fruit
entries.text: His plans may proceed smoothly, and his external machinery may work steadily ; but without actual fruit in the saving of souls, he counts all these as nothing.
entries.slideText: His plans may proceed smoothly, and his external machinery may work steadily ; but without actual fruit in the saving of souls, he counts all these as nothing.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed discussion prompt about longing for spiritual fruit while remaining faithful in difficult fields.
entries.reviewNote: Do not make visible results the sole measure of faithfulness or imply that every faithful ministry receives immediate conversions.

entries.title: But Christ
entries.text: Not the church, but Christ. Not doctrine, but Christ. Not forms, but Christ.
entries.slideText: Not doctrine, but Christ. Not forms, but Christ.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed Christ-centered contrast against trusting institutions, abstractions, or outward forms in place of Christ.
entries.reviewNote: Do not use the rhetorical contrast to dismiss the local church, sound doctrine, or biblical ordinances. Bonar's point is that none can replace Christ.

entries.title: Seek the Lord early
entries.text: Let us seek the Lord early.
entries.slideText: Let us seek the Lord early.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed prompt for cultivating morning prayer and Scripture meditation.
entries.reviewNote: This is wise devotional counsel, not a rule that makes one hour holier than another. Teach prayer from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: They walked with God
entries.text: They were spiritual men, and walked with God.
entries.slideText: They were spiritual men, and walked with God.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed transition from discussing historic preachers to examining the preacher's own walk with God.
entries.reviewNote: The statement refers to ministers discussed in context. Avoid making reputation or historical success the measure of spirituality.

entries.title: Personal joy in Christ
entries.text: Our power in drawing men to Christ springs chiefly from the fullness of our personal joy in him
entries.slideText: Our power in drawing men to Christ springs chiefly from the fullness of our personal joy in him
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed application about how delight in Christ strengthens sincere Christian witness.
entries.reviewNote: Only the Holy Spirit convicts and draws effectively. Present personal joy as testimony, not a human technique for producing conversion.

entries.title: A ministry of power
entries.text: A ministry of power must be the fruit of a holy, peaceful, loving intimacy with the Lord.
entries.slideText: A ministry of power must be the fruit of a holy, peaceful, loving intimacy with the Lord.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed call to private devotion, prayer, and abiding in Christ before public ministry.
entries.reviewNote: Avoid implying mystical intimacy apart from Scripture or making private experience the source of doctrinal authority.
